title: Auto Loans: Autopay Debit Presented to a Closed Account
content:
Whether a returned autopay debit on an Auto Loans installment was PCB's error turns on the date the paying checking account closed. This note sets out that comparison.

## Rule

From the returned autopay debit two facts are taken: the date it posted and the account it drew on. That account's closing date is then read from the borrower's checking records. PCB error is established when the debit came back unpaid and the account has a closing date that falls earlier than the debit's posting date.

PCB error is not established when no reversal names the debit, when the account had not closed by the posting date (a closing date equal to that date or later), or when the account has no closing date recorded.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical debit posted 10 June 2031 and later reversed)

| When the debited account closed | Outcome |
|---|---|
| 9 June 2031 | established |
| 10 June 2031 | not established, the account was open that day |
| 30 June 2031 | not established |
| no closing date | not established |

If the same debit had never been reversed, none of these rows would establish PCB error.
